Sentinel errors shared by every package of the module. They are usually wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is. Typed errors that carry a PROFINET error code (a PNIO status, a DCP block error, an RPC fault) match one of these as well, so that a caller can test for the class of a failure without knowing the code.

## Types

### type Backoff

```go
type Backoff struct {
	Min, Max time.Duration
	Jitter   float64
}
```

Backoff is an exponential backoff: the wait doubles from Min up to Max, and Jitter (0 to 1) spreads it randomly downward by up to that fraction, so that devices that failed together do not retry together.

#### func (Backoff) Delay

```go
func (b Backoff) Delay(attempt int, r float64) time.Duration
```

Delay returns the wait before the given attempt (1 for the first retry) with r, a random number in \[0, 1), applied to the jitter.

### type ContextLogger

```go
type ContextLogger interface {
	Logger

	DebugContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

ContextLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with context-aware structured logging, so that a handler can pick trace and span identifiers out of the context. When the Logger also implements ContextLogger, entries that belong to a request are logged with the context the request was called with.

### type FieldLogger

```go
type FieldLogger interface {
	Logger

	// With returns a logger that adds the given fields to every entry.
	With(keysAndValues ...any) FieldLogger

	DebugKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

FieldLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with structured key-value logging. When the Logger given to a controller or device also implements FieldLogger, the library logs through it: every entry is a constant message plus fields such as "component", "station", "ar" and "error", instead of one formatted string. [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) returns such a logger.

keysAndValues alternate string keys and values, as in log/slog.

#### func NewSlogFieldLogger

```go
func NewSlogFieldLogger(h slog.Handler) FieldLogger
```

NewSlogFieldLogger is [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) with the result typed as a [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger), for callers that want to add fields with With before handing the logger to a controller or device. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

### type Logger

```go
type Logger interface {
	Debugf(format string, args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warnf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
}
```

Logger is the logging interface accepted by controllers, devices and the protocol engines. Implement it to integrate any logging library.

Logging is silent by default. Methods are invoked synchronously on the protocol path and must not block.

#### func NewSlogLogger

```go
func NewSlogLogger(h slog.Handler) Logger
```

NewSlogLogger wraps a slog.Handler. The result implements [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger) and [ContextLogger](#type-contextlogger), so the library logs structured fields through it; messages are only built when the handler is enabled for their level. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

#### func NewStdLogger

```go
func NewStdLogger(l *log.Logger) Logger
```

NewStdLogger wraps a standard library logger. Each message is prefixed with its level. A nil l logs to os.Stderr with the standard flags.

#### func NopLogger

```go
func NopLogger() Logger
```

NopLogger returns a Logger that discards everything.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnStateChange is called for every state change of a controller's
	// device lifecycle or of a device's AR. err is the failure that
	// caused it, if any.
	OnStateChange(station, from, to string, err error)

	// OnConnect is called when a Connect completed: on a controller when
	// the device answered (or the call failed), on a device when it
	// answered a controller. d is the time the Connect took; err is nil
	// when the AR was established.
	OnConnect(station string, d time.Duration, err error)

	// OnAbort is called when an AR ended without a release: a watchdog,
	// an abort by the peer, a CM activity timeout, a lost link. err
	// matches [ErrAborted] or [ErrTimeout].
	OnAbort(station string, err error)

	// OnRecord is called after a record access: on a controller a
	// ReadRecord, WriteRecord or WriteMultiple call, on a device a request
	// it served. op is "read" or "write"; d the time it took; err nil when
	// it succeeded.
	OnRecord(station, op string, index uint16, d time.Duration, err error)

	// OnAlarm is called for every alarm a controller received or a device
	// sent; typ is the alarm type's name, high its priority.
	OnAlarm(station, typ string, high bool)

	// OnRetry is called when a controller schedules the next connection
	// attempt to a device after a failure: attempt counts the attempts
	// since the device last ran, wait is the backoff before it.
	OnRetry(station string, attempt int, wait time.Duration, err error)
}
```

Metrics is an optional callback interface for observing the application relationships of a controller or a device: their state changes, connects, aborts, record accesses, alarms and reconnection attempts. A nil Metrics disables collection. The counters of each component (OBSERVABILITY.md) complement it.

station names the peer: on a controller the device's NameOfStation, on a device the controller's (CMInitiatorStationName). States are the names the controller's State and the device's ARState print.

The methods are called synchronously on the protocol path, possibly from several goroutines at once; implementations must be safe for concurrent use and must not block (increment a counter, send on a buffered channel). Embed [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics) to implement only the callbacks you need and to stay compatible when methods are added.
